notes: The description does not identify childhood versus concurrent conduct, or distinguish the higher order Constraint trait from its lower order Control component. Table 4 prints both traits against both conduct periods; pp. 1166 and 1172 relate Constraint and Control, respectively, to Big Five Conscientiousness. No unique target can be assigned. Table 4 candidates, printed r against rule-abiding versus antisocial conduct: Constraint childhood .23** and concurrent .28***; Control childhood .21** and concurrent .27***. These are positive-conduct correlations, not correlations with an antisocial-behavior-reversed score. No sign reversal or metric conversion performed. Table 4 significance key: ** p ⬍ .01; *** p ⬍ .001. These bounds belong only to the respective candidate cells, not an assigned target. Conduct scoring is documented on p. 1170 as ranging from poor to good conduct. Table 4 reports correlations, preserving the printed r metric. PDF p. 7 rendered and visually inspected. Only es_value_o is assigned; all other core fields are unassigned placeholders. No analytic N is extracted or derived.
